feedback.author: mosya415
feedback.body: cc @ch-wan (author of the DSA backend + `_dsa_split_backend_resolution`) and @Fridge003 as an attention/DSA CODEOWNER. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` with the tilelang DSA backend on CUDA is accepted silently: the server boots fully and then crashes at decode CUDA-graph capture with `kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn`, because the CUDA `tilelang_sparse_fwd` path hardcodes bf16 KV (the fp8 path only exists under `if _is_hip:`). This adds a fail-fast in `_dsa_split_backend_resolution` guarded by `is_hip()` so the ROCm path is unaffected, plus a CPU-only unit test. Auto-resolution never selects tilelang on CUDA, so only an explicit backend is guarded. Could someone add the `run-ci` label and take a look? Thanks!

feedback.author: mosya415
feedback.body:
I have updated the description with a hardware reproduction on H100.

The failure is now confirmed twice on unmodified upstream builds. At the kernel level, `tilelang_sparse_fwd` returns normally with a bfloat16 KV cache and raises `kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn` with an fp8_e4m3 one, everything else being identical. At the server level, on a DSA model running across 4 nodes of 8x H100 with tilelang for prefill and decode, changing only the KV cache dtype from bfloat16 to fp8_e4m3 reproduces the same error, and the traceback confirms it happens during decode CUDA-graph capture, after the full model load.

Could a maintainer add the `run-ci` label? Right now the whole test matrix is skipped, and the two aggregate jobs then report failure, so the PR looks red even though nothing has actually run.

cc @ch-wan @Fridge003

feedback.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor flashinfer-cubin before rejecting FP4**

In CUDA installs that include the precompiled `flashinfer-cubin` package but omit `nvcc` (the same package that `has_flashinfer()` already treats as sufficient to avoid local JIT), this new helper returns `False` because it only accepts `flashinfer_jit_cache` or a local CUDA 12.8+ compiler. That makes `_supports_quant_scheme()` reject the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 schemes, so explicit `--moe-backend=flashinfer_cutlass` NVFP4/MXFP4 deployments fail selection even though the precompiled cubins are available.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

feedback.author: dumko2001
feedback.body: Closing after re-auditing this against the producer rather than maintaining a vLLM-side package/toolchain heuristic. The current branch is incorrect because flashinfer-cubin does not provide the CUTLASS fused_moe JIT module, so its early return still accepts the reported broken installation. More importantly, FlashInfer merged flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3738, which removes the CUDA 12.8 dependency for the Hopper MXFP4 path by using CUTLASS subbyte FP4 types. That is the durable fix for the H100 report; vLLM should consume it through a future FlashInfer pin instead of probing private JIT-cache/package details. flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3951 can remain open for a public capability API and clearer diagnostics. #48541 should remain open until vLLM pins a release containing #3738 and validates the original repro.
